title: Policy-based text redaction
description: Redact sensitive spans from a dataset of texts according to per-record policy statements, balancing under-redaction (leaks) against over-redaction (unreadable output), and scoring the result against a 5-criterion rubric.

cta.label: Fork and run
cta.note: Runs on Jetty's managed sandbox. No setup. Free for your first 10 runs.

example_outputs.title: 10 professional-domain records (healthcare, education, legal)
example_outputs.summary: Clinic emails, a discharge summary, school counselor notes, and privileged legal memos — each redacted against its own policy list. Scored 4.8/5 in a single pass: 5/5 on policy compliance, context preservation, marker consistency and readability, 4/5 on precision (two legal memos redact whole strategy sentences by design). Numbered markers keep who-said-what-to-whom intact.

outputs.description: All 10 records with original fields plus redacted_text (96 labelled markers across the set).
Rubric scores with per-criterion justification, per-record notes, iteration history.
Stage results, structured rubric scores, overall_score 4.8, overall_passed.

example_outputs.title: 8 support & community records (e-commerce, forum, fintech)
example_outputs.summary: Chat transcripts with card digits, order and tracking numbers, a parenting forum post naming a child's allergy and preschool, a fintech call summary with balances and a transaction reference — each redacted against its own policy list. 70 labelled markers, zero leaks on spot-check, rubric 5.0/5 in a single 3-minute pass.

outputs.description: All 8 records with original fields plus redacted_text (70 labelled markers across the set).
Rubric scores with per-criterion justification, per-record notes, iteration history.
Stage results, structured rubric scores, overall_score 5.0, overall_passed.

example_outputs.title: 20-record sample (government, corporation, individual)
example_outputs.summary: The original 20-record dataset — Enron-style corporate email threads, government notices, personal writing — re-run on the current runbook: 216 labelled markers across the set, entities numbered per record so forwarded threads stay readable, scored 4.2/5 (marker consistency 5, everything else 4) in a single pass with a well-formed validation report.

outputs.description: All 20 records with original fields plus redacted_text (216 labelled markers).
Run summary with rubric scores and iteration history.
Stage results, structured rubric scores, overall_score 4.2, overall_passed.

inputs.label: Input dataset
inputs.description: JSON array of records, each with id, domain, policy, policy_ids, and text.

inputs.label: Redaction marker style
inputs.description: Format for replacing sensitive spans, e.g. [REDACTED: PERSON].

metrics._note: Live counters — supplied by the Jetty backend at render time, not authored here.

caveats: The sample run's input dataset draws on Enron-style corporate correspondence for the `corporation` domain records.
Rubric scores are self-assessed by the agent per Step 4 of the runbook, not independently verified by a separate judge model.

v1.0.3 pins the validation_report.json stage shape to {name, passed, message} and asserts it in the final checklist: two earlier runs on the 20-record sample wrote {stage, status: 'completed'} entries, which the Jetty dashboard renders as zero checks passed even though the run succeeded.
